history.dynasty: None (built under the Sikkimese monarchy, Chogyal era)
history.summary: FLAG - NOT A HINDU TEMPLE: Do Drul Chorten is a Buddhist stupa of the Nyingma order of Tibetan Buddhism at Deorali, Gangtok - keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset. The site was once considered haunted, and the young Chogyal of Sikkim invited Trulshik Rinpoche, head of the Nyingma order, from Tibet to consecrate it and dispel negative influences. Construction began in 1945 and was completed the following year. Trulshik Rinpoche placed in the central chamber a complete Dorjee Phurba mandala set, volumes of the Kangyur (canonical Tibetan Buddhist scriptures), long rolls of mantras (zung), and other ritual objects, making it a powerful protective monument and one of Sikkim's most important stupas. It is encircled by 108 Mani Lhakor (prayer wheels) and surrounded by Chorten Lakhang and Guru Lakhang housing two statues of Guru Rinpoche; a monastery for young lamas stands beside it with large images of Padmasambhava and his manifestation Guru Snang Sid Zilzon.

name: Do Drul Chorten
town_description: Gangtok is the capital of Sikkim, a hill town at about 1,650 m. The stupa stands on Deorali hill, about 500 m above the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.
